title: TS SDK: single-source streaming primitives for for-await and ReadableStream consumers
creator: Miguel Ortega
description:
Problem: SDK currently exposes multiple diverging streaming entry points (async iterables in Node examples, ReadableStream in browser examples, and separate helper adapters). Consumers are confused about which primitive to use for new integrations. This ticket standardizes on a single SDK primitive that: (1) is ergonomic for for-await (Node and Deno), (2) provides a first-class conversion to browser ReadableStream/ReadableStreamDefaultReader, and (3) supports cancellation, backpressure propagation, and resume semantics.

Goal: Implement a StreamingResponse abstraction that is the canonical return type for streaming endpoints in the TypeScript SDK. StreamingResponse should implement AsyncIterable<string | Uint8Array> and expose a .toReadableStream() method for browsers and a .asNodeReadable() helper for Node when necessary. The implementation must ensure: token-level backpressure hooks (where feasible), clear cancellation semantics (abort controller integration), and deterministic finalization so user code can await stream completion.

Why this matters: Many customers run hybrid apps (server + web) and expect identical semantics across runtimes. Having a single source-of-truth primitive reduces docs surface area, prevents subtle memory leaks, and enables a single set of tests validating retry/resume behavior across consumer APIs.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce StreamingResponse type exported from SDK that implements AsyncIterable
Implement .toReadableStream() which returns a WHATWG ReadableStream in browsers and compatible runtimes
Provide .getReader() / .toNodeAsyncIterator() compatibility helpers documented in the README
Cancellation via AbortSignal must stop further network requests and release KV cache references
Backpressure behavior documented: SDK must not prebuffer more than X tokens beyond consumer pull (configurable default)
Unit + integration tests covering for-await consumption, ReadableStream piping to TransformStream, and cancelation from both sides
Migration guide added to SDK docs with code snippets for common patterns
proposed_api_examples: const resp = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-1.4', messages });
for await (const chunk of resp) { console.log(chunk.text ?? chunk); }
// Browser: pipe to DOM WritableStream or use streaming decode
// Or pipe to a TransformStream for decoding: readable.pipeThrough(myDecoder).pipeTo(writable);
const resp = await client.chat.stream({ ..., signal: ac.signal });
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 5000); // stop early - network aborted and SDK finalizes stream
const nodeStream = resp.asNodeReadable(); // returns stream.Readable for older Node codepaths
migration_notes: Existing methods that return raw AsyncGenerator or ad-hoc Web Streams should be deprecated in favor of returning StreamingResponse. Provide a light shim layer in this release so older examples still work: const streaming = StreamingResponse.from(rawIterator) and const streaming = StreamingResponse.fromReadable(myReadableStream). Deprecation warning in console/logs for one minor release before removal.
tradeoffs: Single primitive simplifies docs and tests but requires extra code to support legacy Node Readable compatibility (we'll provide small adapters)
Eager buffering reduces latency variance but increases memory; default will be conservative (buffer_limit_tokens=8) and configurable
Implementing full pull-driven hardware-backed backpressure is complex across browsers/Node; we emulate by pausing network prefetch and honoring consumer pulls where possible

2025-11-13 Samantha Li: Picking this up for implementation. Will drive a small state machine to manage pull/push states and integrate AbortSignal. Plan to land core in a feature branch and iterate on adapters.
2025-11-15 Priya Kapoor (review): Question on toReadableStream() semantics — do we expose strategy.size hooks? Prefer keeping enqueue sizes opaque for now; add advanced hooks in a follow-up.

2025-11-17 Rajiv Menon (networking): We need transport support to pause prefetch when consumer backpressure happens. I'll add a hook to the transport layer (pausePrefetch(tokenCount)) and a metrics event for prefetch depth.
